newsitem.title: GABON: Gabon opposition leader becomes mayor of capital.
newsitem.headline: Gabon opposition leader becomes mayor of capital.

text.p: Opposition leader Father Paul Mba Abessole is the new mayor of Gabon's capital Libreville, after his National Woodcutters' Rally won municipal elections there in October.
Abessole, a Roman Catholic priest who was formally elected mayor on Sunday, said on state television on Monday he would ask for an exhaustive audit of the city's affairs.
"An audit of Libreville must be carried out... I want this audit to be exhaustive," he added.
The October election was the first significant gain by the opposition since moves towards democracy began with a national conference in 1990.
But President Omar Bongo's ruling Democratic Party won a comfortable majority in the 120-seat national assembly in subsequent December parliamentary election, including most seats in Libreville.

Abessole, runner-up to Bongo in disputed 1993 elections, said his priorities for Libreville were a clean, beautiful, lively and prosperous town. "That sums up everything, from the economic and the social point of view," he said.

The elections were part of a democratic timetable brokered in Paris in 1994 after political violence shook the oil-producing Central African nation following the 1993 presidential election, killing over a dozen people.
They were Gabon's second multiparty legislative polls. The first were in 1990 when a wave of democratic reform swept across Africa after the fall of Soviet-bloc communism.
Bongo has ruled the former French colony since 1968 after the death of Gabon's founding head of state, Leon Mba. His presidential term ends in 1998.
